**Short answer**  
The statutes supplied (UAPA 1967 and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023) define terrorist acts and prescribe punishments but do not enumerate any specific statutory defences. Consequently, a person accused of terrorism must rely on general criminal‑law defences (e.g., lack of intent, mistaken identity, alibi, duress, or statutory exceptions) and on procedural safeguards under the Criminal Procedure Code (now the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Criminal Procedure Code, 2024). The sources provided do not contain any explicit defence provisions; relevant case law or commentary would be needed to identify recognised defences.
